title: The Kiosk Couldn't Log In — So Its Calendar Stayed Empty | vitalii.no
description:
A family calendar strip on a kitchen TV stayed nearly empty, because Google Calendar events only exist inside a browser that's signed in — and a TV kiosk that never logs in to anything could never show them, even though most of the family's actual schedule lived there.

The kiosk's calendar endpoint now fetches events from a calendar server in parallel with its existing database and sports-club sources, merging all three into one list. Google-sourced events are detected automatically and colored a distinct green alongside the existing sources, with counts of each reported for diagnostics. Events with no assigned family member — most of the Google entries — now render as a full-width banner instead of being silently dropped for having nowhere to sit.

Three separate sources, one real week: nothing that used to vanish disappears anymore.
